title: ICP monitoring in paediatric traumatic brain injury

speakers.name: Dr Ramzi Hamzeh
speakers.role: Consultant in Paediatric Intensive Care at the Royal London Hospital

summary: A ten-year single-centre review of intracranial pressure monitoring in severe childhood brain injury, and why multicentre research is needed.
description:
Dr Ramzi Hamzeh, Consultant in Paediatric Intensive Care at the Royal London Hospital, provides insights into a retrospective single-centre review of severe traumatic brain injury in children. He describes how the team examined admissions and the use of intracranial pressure monitoring over a ten-year period. The interview raises questions about which patients receive monitoring, how decisions are made and what can be learned from outcomes in the local cohort. Dr Hamzeh emphasises the limitations of a single-centre retrospective analysis and the need for further multicentre research to better understand patient selection and monitoring strategies in paediatric intensive care.

This interview took place at the PCCS Annual Scientific Meeting 2026 in London.

title: Transition from PICU to adult critical care

speakers.name: Professor Natalie Pattison
speakers.role: Professor of Clinical Nursing at Imperial College London

summary: How adult services can prepare to receive young people from paediatric intensive care, and why young people and families should shape the plan.
description:
Professor Natalie Pattison, Professor of Clinical Nursing at Imperial College London, provides insights into the transition from paediatric intensive care to adult critical care. She discusses the preparation adult services need to receive young people, including appropriate resources, staff training and named transition leads. The interview highlights the importance of a structured, shared approach between services while recognising that each person's circumstances and preferences are different. Professor Pattison emphasises involving young people themselves, as well as their families, and understanding what matters to them when planning where and how their care is delivered.

This interview took place at the PCCS Annual Scientific Meeting 2026 in London.

title: Recognising deterioration before PICU admission

speakers.name: Dr Emer Kennedy
speakers.role: Resident Doctor

speakers.name: Jack Ramsay
speakers.role: Medical Student at Newcastle University

summary: A two-cycle audit of how deterioration is recognised and escalated before unplanned PICU admission, and what it means for an outreach service.
description:
Dr Emer Kennedy, Resident Doctor, and Jack Ramsay, Medical Student at Newcastle University, discuss an audit of the recognition and response to deterioration before unplanned admission to paediatric intensive care. They describe work at Great North Children’s Hospital examining escalation, clinical response and documentation across two audit cycles. The interview explores changes observed over time and the contribution of a paediatric deterioration nurse specialist. They reflect on how the findings can support the development of a critical-care outreach service and describe plans to continue evaluating this area of care.

This interview took place at the PCCS Annual Scientific Meeting 2026 in London.

title: A parent’s perspective on shaping critical-care research

speakers.name: Amy Dent
speakers.role: Community Partner at Imperial College London

summary: How a parent contributes lived experience through patient and public involvement to help shape paediatric critical-care research.
description:
Amy Dent, Community Partner at Imperial College London, shares a parent’s perspective on participating in paediatric critical-care research. She describes how patient and public involvement offers a way to contribute lived experience and help shape the questions and methods used by research teams. The interview explores the importance of flexible, supportive participation and the value of feeling that family perspectives are heard. Amy reflects on giving back through research, working with others and helping develop projects that are relevant to the experiences and priorities of children and their families.

This interview took place at the PCCS Annual Scientific Meeting 2026 in London.

title: Data, AI and clinical decision support in PICU

speakers.name: Dr Samiran Ray
speakers.role: Consultant in Paediatric Intensive Care at Great Ormond Street Hospital

summary: How PICU data repositories and decision-support tools could help clinicians weigh uncertainty while supporting, not replacing, clinical judgement.
description:
Dr Samiran Ray, Consultant in Paediatric Intensive Care at Great Ormond Street Hospital, provides insights into the role of data and artificial intelligence in paediatric critical care. He describes the volume of information generated by bedside monitors, electronic health records and clinical interactions, and the challenge of bringing it together to support decisions. The interview explores the development of data repositories through collaboration between clinical, engineering and mathematical teams. Dr Ray considers how future decision-support tools could help clinicians assess uncertainty and understand patterns in critical illness, supporting rather than replacing clinical judgement.

This interview took place at the PCCS Annual Scientific Meeting 2026 in London.

title: What makes paediatric critical care trials succeed?

speakers.name: Professor Kathy Rowan
speakers.role: Founder and Scientific Advisor at ICNARC

summary: The collaborative culture, methodology and data quality behind the UK's randomised trials in paediatric critical care.
description:
Professor Kathy Rowan, Founder and Scientific Advisor at ICNARC, provides insights into the achievements of the UK paediatric critical care community in delivering randomised clinical trials. She reflects on the collaborative culture behind this work and the contribution of expertise in methodology, data and analysis. The interview highlights the importance of high-quality trial delivery, including complete data collection and adherence to the interventions being evaluated. Professor Rowan explains how these shared efforts have helped produce a substantial evidence base and enabled findings from paediatric critical care research to reach an international audience through major scientific publications.

This interview took place at the PCCS Annual Scientific Meeting 2026 in London.

title: Oncology outcomes in PICU: trends and future research

speakers.name: Professor Jonathan Round
speakers.role: Professor of Practice in Clinical Education and Consultant Paediatric Intensivist

summary: Long-term PICANet trends in oncology admissions to intensive care, how to interpret them, and plans for the Care PICU study.
description:
Professor Jonathan Round, Professor of Practice in Clinical Education and Consultant Paediatric Intensivist, provides insights into long-term trends in oncology admissions to paediatric intensive care. He describes the METRO research group's use of PICANet data to explore changes in mortality, admission numbers and illness severity. The interview considers how these trends should be interpreted, including the possible contribution of changing admission thresholds and patient selection. Professor Round also discusses questions that remain about this patient group and introduces plans for the Care PICU study, which aims to examine pathways into intensive care and subsequent outcomes in greater detail.

This interview took place at the PCCS Annual Scientific Meeting 2026 in London.

title: Shared adult and paediatric expertise in adolescent trauma

speakers.name: Ms Maryam Alfa-Wali
speakers.role: Consultant Colorectal and Trauma Surgeon

summary: Why adolescent major trauma care benefits from combining adult and paediatric expertise, including safeguarding and support through recovery.
description:
Ms Maryam Alfa-Wali, Consultant Colorectal and Trauma Surgeon, provides insights into the care of adolescents with major trauma and the debate about adult and paediatric settings. She discusses the value of bringing expertise from both services together, including adult teams' experience of treating major injuries and paediatric teams' understanding of younger patients' needs. The interview explores safeguarding, developmental differences and the support teenagers may require during recovery. Ms Alfa-Wali argues for a shared approach that looks beyond the injury itself and draws on the strengths of both specialties to care for the young person as a whole.

This interview took place at the PCCS Annual Scientific Meeting 2026 in London.

title: Reducing low-value care in paediatric ICU

speakers.name: Professor Lyvonne Tume
speakers.role: Professor of Critical Care Nursing

summary: A Delphi study of low-value PICU practices such as routine blood sampling and fasting, and why questioning routine care matters.
description:
Professor Lyvonne Tume, Professor of Critical Care Nursing, discusses a multidisciplinary study identifying low-value practices in paediatric intensive care. She explains how a Delphi process brought together professional perspectives on interventions that may be unnecessary or offer limited benefit. Topics include routine blood sampling, medication review, fasting and the influence of risk aversion on everyday decisions. The interview explores why reducing low-value care matters for children and families as well as staff workload, resources and the environment. Professor Tume encourages teams to examine the evidence behind routine practice and consider where change could improve care.

This interview took place at the PCCS Annual Scientific Meeting 2026 in London.

title: Precision medicine in intensive care

speakers.name: Professor Anthony Gordon MBE
speakers.role: Professor of Anaesthesia and Critical Care at Imperial College London

summary: How biomarkers could identify patients with different biological responses to critical illness and help design trials across adult and paediatric care.
description:
Professor Anthony Gordon MBE, Professor of Anaesthesia and Critical Care at Imperial College London, discusses the potential of precision medicine in adult and paediatric intensive care. He explains how patients with similar clinical presentations may have different underlying biological responses, creating challenges for treatment and research. The interview explores the use of RNA and protein biomarkers, the prospect of bedside measurement and approaches to identifying which treatments may benefit particular groups of patients. Professor Gordon reflects on designing studies around these differences and the opportunities for collaboration across adult and paediatric critical care.

This interview took place at the PCCS Annual Scientific Meeting 2026 in London.

title: Acute liver failure: supporting recovery without transplant

speakers.name: Professor Akash Deep
speakers.role: Professor of Paediatric Critical Care and Director of PICU at King's College Hospital

summary: How critical care can support some children with acute liver failure to recover without transplant, from treating the cause to extracorporeal therapies.
description:
Professor Akash Deep, Professor of Paediatric Critical Care and Director of PICU at King's College Hospital, provides insights into supporting children with acute liver failure. He reflects on the development of liver transplantation and discusses approaches that may help some children recover without needing a transplant, depending on the underlying cause. The interview covers identifying and treating the cause of liver failure, neurological monitoring and protection, and the role of extracorporeal therapies. Professor Deep highlights the importance of timely, coordinated critical care in supporting recovery while recognising that the clinical approach depends on the individual child's condition.

This interview took place at the PCCS Annual Scientific Meeting 2026 in London.

title: Caring for teenagers after major trauma

speakers.name: Professor Akash Deep
speakers.role: Professor of Paediatric Critical Care and Director of PICU at King's College Hospital

summary: Why care for teenagers after major trauma should look beyond the injury to safeguarding, psychosocial support, family involvement and recovery.
description:
Professor Akash Deep, Professor of Paediatric Critical Care and Director of PICU at King's College Hospital, provides insights into the debate about where teenagers should receive care after major trauma. He argues that the discussion must extend beyond the immediate injury, resuscitation and surgery to consider the young person's broader needs. The interview explores safeguarding, psychosocial support, family involvement and recovery back into everyday life. Professor Deep advocates an integrated approach that brings the appropriate expertise to the patient, recognising that adolescence is a period of continuing development and that care should support the whole journey of recovery.

This interview took place at the PCCS Annual Scientific Meeting 2026 in London.

title: Understanding extubation failure in children

speakers.name: Dr Becky Mitting
speakers.role: Consultant in Paediatric Intensive Care at St Mary’s Hospital

description:
Dr Becky Mitting, Consultant in Paediatric Intensive Care at St Mary’s Hospital, discusses her PhD research into extubation failure in children. She describes using PICANet registry data to explore factors associated with the need for further breathing support after extubation. The interview considers the limits of prediction using the information currently available and the importance of understanding the experience of children and families. Dr Mitting reflects on what the work has revealed, the questions that remain and potential directions for research aimed at improving the assessment and prevention of extubation failure.

This interview took place at the PCCS Annual Scientific Meeting 2026 in London.

title: Onc Around the Clock: timing of oncology PICU admissions

speakers.name: Professor Jonathan Round
speakers.role: Professor of Practice in Clinical Education and Consultant Paediatric Intensivist

summary: How admission patterns and mortality for unplanned oncology PICU admissions vary by time of day, and what the data can and cannot show.
description:
Professor Jonathan Round, Professor of Practice in Clinical Education and Consultant Paediatric Intensivist, provides insights into research examining the timing of unplanned oncology admissions to paediatric intensive care. Drawing on PICANet data, he describes differences in admission patterns and mortality across the day and night. He explores possible explanations, including variation in admission decisions and patient selection, while distinguishing these hypotheses from conclusions the available data can establish. The interview highlights the value of large datasets in identifying questions for further investigation and the need for prospective research to understand the pathways and outcomes of children with cancer who require intensive care.

This interview took place at the PCCS Annual Scientific Meeting 2026 in London.

title: Reducing delays in ventilation weaning in PICU

speakers.role: Foundation Year 1 Doctor

summary: A retrospective audit of delays in ventilation weaning in PICU and how a checklist or electronic-record dashboard could help teams.
description:
Dr Wardah Ahmad, Foundation Year 1 Doctor, provides insights into a retrospective audit of ventilation weaning in a paediatric intensive care unit, undertaken during her medical studies. She describes how the project examined delays in starting and sustaining weaning, alongside the consistency of related assessments and documentation. The interview explores how audit findings can identify opportunities to support staff and improve the reliability of clinical processes. Dr Ahmad discusses possible next steps, including a checklist or protocol and an electronic-record dashboard to help teams recognise when relevant criteria have been met and consider the next stage of care.

title: Lessons from Grenfell: supporting healthcare staff wellbeing

speakers.name: Dr Anu Mitra
speakers.role: Consultant in Emergency Medicine

summary: Reflections on leading an emergency department response to a major incident and what it taught about supporting healthcare staff wellbeing.
description:
Dr Anu Mitra, Consultant in Emergency Medicine, provides insights into his experience of the Grenfell Tower fire response and the impact of major incidents on healthcare staff. He reflects on unexpectedly leading the emergency-department response, the emotional demands of the night and his own process of recovery. The interview explores how these experiences informed his thinking about staff wellbeing more widely, including practical support, opportunities for reflection and recognising colleagues' contributions. Dr Mitra emphasises kindness and compassion within healthcare teams, and the importance of caring for ourselves and one another while caring for patients.

title: Transition to adult care: The Inbetweeners

speakers.role: Consultant Paediatrician and Lead Clinical Co-ordinator for Child Health at NCEPOD

summary: Findings and recommendations from a national study of transition to adult services for young people with complex conditions, and progress since.
description:
Dr Katherine (Katie) Malbon, Consultant Paediatrician and Lead Clinical Co-ordinator for Child Health at NCEPOD, provides insights into The Inbetweeners study and the transition from paediatric to adult services for young people with complex conditions. She discusses gaps in the organisation and delivery of transition care, including staff training, involvement of young people and coordination between specialties. The interview explores recommendations for making developmentally appropriate healthcare part of everyday practice, strengthening multidisciplinary working and ensuring transition has organisational support. Dr Malbon also reflects on the progress reported by services since the study and the importance of keeping young people's needs at the centre of change.

This interview took place at the PCCS Annual Scientific Meeting 2026 in London.

title: Young people shaping critical-care research

speakers.role: Community Partner at Imperial College London

Libby Scarlet Watkins, Community Partner at Imperial College London, discusses why young people should have a voice in critical-care research. Drawing on her experience as a former paediatric intensive-care patient, she explains how involvement in research has offered a positive way to contribute and connect with others. The interview explores the skills and confidence that participation can develop, including considering research ideas and sharing personal perspectives. Libby highlights the value of meeting peers with related experiences and encourages research teams to create opportunities for more young people to take part.

This interview took place at the PCCS Annual Scientific Meeting 2026 in London.

title: How paediatric ARDS research differs from adult evidence

speakers.name: Dr Becky Mitting
speakers.role: Consultant in Paediatric Intensive Care at St Mary’s Hospital

summary: Why adult findings on acute respiratory distress syndrome cannot simply be applied to children, and the role of precision medicine in future studies.
description:
Dr Becky Mitting, Consultant in Paediatric Intensive Care at St Mary’s Hospital, reflects on discussions comparing adult and paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome research. She explores why findings from adult studies cannot automatically be applied to children, considering differences in lung physiology and the available trial evidence. The interview highlights questions raised by a joint conference session and the potential role of more targeted research. Dr Mitting discusses the opportunities offered by precision medicine while emphasising the need to understand paediatric illness on its own terms when developing future studies.

title: Learning from every child: the PIVOTAL platform trial

speakers.role: Professor of Paediatric Intensive Care at UCL and Great Ormond Street Hospital and Chief Investigator of the PIVOTAL platform trial

summary: How a Bayesian adaptive platform trial tests sedation, fluid and transfusion questions together and learns from every child admitted.
description:
Professor Mark Peters, Professor of Paediatric Intensive Care at UCL and Great Ormond Street Hospital and Chief Investigator of the PIVOTAL platform trial, provides insights into the trial’s approach to questions of routine care. He discusses the choice of sedative agents, intravenous fluid strategies and blood-transfusion thresholds. The interview explores how a Bayesian adaptive platform can evaluate several questions at the same time, learn from accumulating information and potentially introduce new questions as others are answered. Professor Peters reflects on the ambition to make research part of learning from every child admitted to intensive care.

This interview took place at the PCCS Annual Scientific Meeting 2026 in London.

title: Bedside resuscitation teaching in PICU

speakers.name: Dr Janapriya Sugumar
speakers.role: Paediatric Registrar and PICSTAR National Trainee Education Lead

summary: A quality-improvement project using short tea-trolley sessions to refresh resuscitation skills at the bedside in a busy PICU.

Dr Janapriya Sugumar, Paediatric Registrar and PICSTAR National Trainee Education Lead, provides insights into an educational quality-improvement project designed to refresh resuscitation skills in a busy paediatric intensive care unit. The interview covers work on basic life support, intraosseous access and tracheostomy management, alongside the importance of frequent opportunities to practise. Dr Sugumar discusses staff engagement, confidence and knowledge, and reflects on how brief, accessible sessions can help sustain multidisciplinary education when clinical services are under pressure.

This interview took place at the PCCS Annual Scientific Meeting 2026 in London.

title: Understanding early unplanned PICU readmission

speakers.role: Senior PICU Fellow in Southampton

Mohamed Elsayed, Senior PICU Fellow in Southampton, discusses research into unplanned readmission to paediatric intensive care within 48 hours of discharge. Mohamed reflects on how understanding readmission can inform quality improvement and help teams examine the safety of care transitions, while recognising the limitations of the study and the need for further work.

speakers.role: Founder and Scientific Advisor at ICNARC

summary: How adaptive platform trials such as PIVOTAL can test several interventions at once and generate evidence for critically ill children faster.

Professor Kathy Rowan, Founder and Scientific Advisor at ICNARC, provides insights into the future of paediatric critical care research through adaptive platform trials. The interview discusses PIVOTAL and the potential for this model to help generate evidence about care for critically ill children more quickly. Professor Rowan also reflects on the collective contribution of the paediatric critical care community and the collaborative delivery that underpins this next stage of clinical research.

title: Rethinking gastric residual monitoring in PICU

speakers.role: Professor of Critical Care Nursing

Professor Lyvonne Tume, Professor of Critical Care Nursing, provides insights into the GASTRIC-PICU trial and the value of questioning established routines in paediatric intensive care. She discusses the study of gastric residual monitoring during enteral feeding and the outcomes that matter to children, families and staff. The interview considers the potential consequences of continuing practices without clear evidence of benefit, including their effect on nutrition, staff time and patient care. Professor Tume reflects on how research can help teams reconsider familiar procedures and identify care that may no longer be necessary.

Dr Ikechukwu Okongwu, Paediatric Registrar at Addenbrooke's Hospital and PICU GRID trainee, provides insights into PICUlearn, an online learning community for paediatric intensive care. Dr Okongwu discusses the value of participation and feedback from across the multidisciplinary team, and his ambition to build a shared space for learning and professional development.

speakers.role: Lead Respiratory Physiotherapist in PICU at Birmingham Children’s Hospital and PCCS Council AHP Representative

speakers.role: Consultant in Paediatric Intensive Care and National Paediatric Organ Donation Lead

Dr Omer Aziz, Consultant in Paediatric Intensive Care and National Paediatric Organ Donation Lead, discusses the partnership between PCCS and NHS Blood and Transplant. speakers.role: Educator with the Yorkshire and Humber Paediatric Critical Care Operational Delivery Network

Arun Ghose, PCCS Communications Lead and Intensive Care Consultant at Birmingham Children’s Hospital, discusses communication and advocacy across the paediatric critical-care community.
