title: Ryan's Rule: patient centric care

speakers.name: Professor Nitin Kapur
speakers.role: President, Paediatric & Child Health Division, Royal Australasian College of Physicians

summary: Why Ryan's Rule matters for patient-centric care, and the importance of listening to patients and families when making clinical decisions.
description: Professor Nitin Kapur; President, Paediatric & Child Health Division, Royal Australasian College of Physicians, discusses Ryan’s Rule and its significance in promoting patient-centric care within the healthcare system. Professor Kapur emphasises the importance of listening to patients and their families and integrating their perspectives into clinical decision-making. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2025 in Glasgow, Scotland.

title: Lessons from the first 100 years of the first university chair of child health in the UK

speakers.name: Professor Faisal Ahmed
speakers.role: Holder of the Samson Gemmell Chair of Child Health at the University of Glasgow

summary: Lessons from a century of the UK's first university chair of child health on how academic leadership and sustained investment have shaped paediatric care.
description: Professor Faisal Ahmed, holder of the Samson Gemmell Chair of Child Health at the University of Glasgow, shares his expertise on advancing paediatric care and research, as a collective healthcare community. Reflecting on his latest publication on the lessons from the first 100 years of the first university chair of child health in the UK, this interview highlights how academic leadership and sustained investment in child health research have shaped the evolution of paediatric medicine and improved outcomes for children worldwide This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2025 in Glasgow, Scotland.

title: RCPCH research priorities

speakers.name: Professor Paul Dimitri
speakers.role: Vice President for Science and Research at the Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health (RCPCH)

summary: How a national Child Health Research group set priority areas, including obesity and mental health, and presented them to the NIHR to support research capacity.
description: Professor Paul Dimitri, Vice President for Science and Research at the Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health (RCPCH), discusses the establishment of a national Child Health Research group focused on identifying and prioritising key areas in paediatric research. Through collaboration with key stakeholders, including RCPCH members and young people, the group identified priority areas such as safeguarding, obesity, mental health, neurodevelopmental paediatrics, and the integration of social care and public health. By presenting these priorities to the NIHR Strategy Board, dedicated funding and support for capacity building in child health research is prioritised. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2025 in Glasgow, UK.

title: Asthma and allergy in children: evaluating outcomes across ethnicity and socioeconomic status

speakers.name: Jordan Nicolle
speakers.role: Paediatric nurse at Brighton and Sussex Medical School

summary: A service evaluation of over 300 patient notes finds some ethnic groups have more severe asthma and more A&E attendances, with next steps to explore barriers.
description: Jordan Nicolle, paediatric nurse at Brighton and Sussex Medical School, provides insights into a service evaluation project focused on asthma and allergy in children and young people. The discussion highlights findings from a retrospective review of over 300 patient notes, examining clinical outcomes and A&E attendances in relation to ethnicity and socioeconomic status. The evaluation found that certain ethnic groups were more likely to have more severe asthma, as measured by an asthma severity scale, and were also more likely to present to A&E. Jordan Nicolle emphasizes the importance of understanding these differences and outlines the next steps, which include exploring barriers to accessing asthma and allergy clinics and investigating the experiences of parents and carers. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2025 in Glasgow, Scotland.

title: Involvement of underserved communities in paediatric genomic testing

speakers.name: Dr Shivani Sekar
speakers.role: East and North Hertfordshire NHS Trust

summary: The barriers underserved communities face at each stage of genomic testing and research, and why reporting study demographics helps address them.
description: Dr Shivani Sekar, East and North Hertfordshire NHS Trust, provides insights into the involvement of underserved communities in paediatric genomic testing, as part of an East of England research team. The discussion highlights the barriers faced by these communities at every stage of the patient pathway; from referral and consent to participation in genomic testing and research reporting. Dr Sekar emphasises the importance of reporting demographic characteristics of study populations to better analyse and address these barriers. She encourages leveraging identified solutions to improve participation and ensure that genomic testing and research are accessible and inclusive for all children and families. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2025 in Glasgow, Scotland.

title: Standardising paediatric oral fluid challenges

speakers.name: Dr Rosie Roots
speakers.role: Paediatrician at Evelina London Children’s Hospital

summary: A multi-site survey shows wide variation in how oral fluid challenges are done in London, and why standard protocols could reduce unnecessary admissions.
description: Dr Rosie Roots, a paediatrician at Evelina London Children’s Hospital, provides insights into a collaborative project examining the process for paediatric oral fluid challenges across the London region, in partnership with the REACH research network. The discussion highlights the significant variation in how these challenges are conducted—including differences in clinical indications, protocols, and criteria for success—and how this impacts patient outcomes. Dr Roots details the findings from a multi-site survey, which confirmed widespread inconsistency in practice and limited adherence to local and national guidelines. She emphasises the importance of standardising oral fluid challenge protocols to improve the success rate and reduce unnecessary hospital admissions. The next phase of the project involves a systematic review to identify best practice recommendations for dissemination across the region. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2025 in Glasgow, Scotland.

title: Transforming waiting times into educational opportunities: the PED TV project

speakers.name: Dr Noellie Mottershead
speakers.role: Consultant in paediatric emergency medicine

speakers.name: Dr Salima Yasmin
speakers.role: Trainee on the Greater Manchester Deprivation Programme

summary: How educational videos and digital posters in a paediatric emergency waiting room improved families' knowledge and confidence, with plans to expand.
description: Dr Noellie Mottershead, consultant in paediatric emergency medicine, and Dr Salima Yasmin, trainee on the Greater Manchester Deprivation Programme, provide insights into the PED TV project—an initiative aimed at transforming waiting times in the paediatric emergency department into valuable educational experiences. The discussion highlights how the team introduced educational videos and digital posters into the waiting room, targeting over 50,000 children and their families each year. By surveying staff, patients, and carers, the project identified key topics such as health promotion and injury prevention, and curated content suitable for children with a reading age of about eight. The initiative resulted in improved knowledge and confidence among families, as well as overwhelmingly positive feedback. Drs Mottershead and Yasmin emphasise the importance of leveraging waiting times for public health education and outline plans to expand the project across Manchester Foundation Trust and potentially to a national scale. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2025 in Glasgow, Scotland.

title: Paired whole genome sequencing for children with suspected cancer

speakers.name: Dr Sarah Leiter
speakers.role: Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

summary: How routine whole genome sequencing can be delivered in clinical care to find genetic changes quickly and guide treatment of suspected childhood cancer.
description: Dr Sarah Leiter, Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, provides insights into the implementation of paired whole genome sequencing (WGS) for children with suspected cancer. The discussion highlights how routine WGS can be delivered as part of clinical care, offering significant benefits by rapidly identifying genetic changes that inform diagnosis and treatment decisions. Dr Leiter emphasises the importance of this approach in improving outcomes for children with suspected cancer, enabling more precise and individualized management strategies. She outlines how integrating WGS into routine clinical pathways can change clinical management and support families facing complex diagnostic journeys. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2025 in Glasgow, Scotland.

title: Building research capacity in paediatric emergency medicine: Assistant Research Practitioners (ARP)

speakers.name: Dr Shrouk Messahel
speakers.role: Consultant in paediatric emergency medicine at Alder Hey Children’s Hospital

summary: How upskilling nursing and healthcare staff as Assistant Research Practitioners increased research recruitment in a busy emergency department.
description: Dr Shrouk Messahel, consultant in paediatric emergency medicine at Alder Hey Children’s Hospital, provides insights into innovative approaches for building research capacity within the emergency department. She highlights the unique challenges of conducting research in a busy, target-driven environment with unscheduled care and ethical considerations around consent in emergencies. Dr Messahel details how her department transformed research delivery by upskilling permanent nursing and healthcare staff into hybrid roles as Assistant Research Practitioners (ARPs), supported by charity funding and embedded within clinical teams. The model increased patient recruitment for key studies—such as STOP RSV—enabled flexible, round-the-clock research activity, and empowered staff to develop new skills and career pathways. Dr Messahel emphasizes the importance of integrating research and clinical work, demonstrating how this approach improves outcomes for children and supports the advancement of emergency medicine. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2025 in Glasgow, Scotland.

title: Medical photography in child protection

speakers.name: Dr Tapomay Banerjee
speakers.role: Consultant paediatrician with Cambridgeshire Community Services NHS Trust

summary: Findings from a community paediatric team on medical photography in child protection examinations, including image quality, peer review and data protection.
description: Dr Tapomay Banerjee, a consultant paediatrician with Cambridgeshire Community Services NHS Trust, provides insights into the implementation and impact of medical photography in child protection work within the Bedford community paediatric team. Dr Banerjee describes the findings of his study which highlights the importance of photographic documentation in child protection examinations, where photographs can convey more information than written descriptions alone. Dr Banerjee details the training received by the team, the audit of 25 children’s photographs, and the positive results regarding image quality, storage security, and the ability of clinicians to accurately identify injuries and body parts. He emphasises the utility of medical photography in peer review and collaboration with social care, while acknowledging ongoing concerns about data protection and acceptability. Dr Banerjee encourages other trusts to adopt similar pathways to enhance child protection practice. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2025 in Glasgow, Scotland.

title: Use of buccal oxycodone in paediatric palliative care

speakers.name: Dr S Suranjana
speakers.role: Specialist in paediatric palliative care at Martin House Children’s Hospice

summary: A small study of oral oxycodone solution given via the buccal route for pain and agitation in children with life-limiting conditions.
description: Dr S Suranjana, a specialist in paediatric palliative care at Martin House Children’s Hospice, provides insights into a research project focused on the use of buccal oxycodone for pain and agitation in children with life-limiting conditions. She highlights the innovative use of standard oral oxycodone solution administered via the buccal route, rather than through enteral tubes, and demonstrates its effectiveness in four patients with neurological and genetic conditions. Dr Suranjana emphasises the importance of flexible, patient-centred approaches in palliative care and outlines how this method could be considered for children who are unable to tolerate enteral administration or who require rapid symptom control. She expresses hope that the study will encourage further research into alternative routes of medication administration to improve comfort and outcomes for children and families. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2025 in Glasgow, Scotland.

title: Innovations and challenges in global vaccination for children

speakers.name: Professor Ed Clarke
speakers.role: Expert in paediatric infection, immunity, and global health

summary: The challenges of reaching children in low- and middle-income countries with vaccines, and new approaches such as micro-needle patches and new vaccines.
description: Professor Ed Clarke, a leading expert in paediatric infection, immunity, and global health, provides insights from his latest research into the major challenges and innovations in global vaccination for children. Professor Clarke highlights two key issues: ensuring that children in low- and middle-income countries receive existing vaccines, such as measles and rubella, which are often missed due to logistical and societal barriers; and developing new vaccines targeted at pathogens that cause significant disease burdens in these regions, such as group A streptococcus and viral hemorrhagic fevers. Professor Clarke emphasises the importance of new technologies like micro-needle patches (recently published), which offer pain-free, easy-to-administer alternatives to traditional injections and help overcome cold chain and training challenges. He outlines how these innovations can improve vaccine coverage and preparedness for future outbreaks, with a particular focus on his work in The Gambia and other resource-limited settings. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2025 in Glasgow, Scotland.

title: Development of cognitive empathy in children with neurological disorders

speakers.name: Professor Liam Dorris
speakers.role: Paediatric neuropsychologist and honorary professor at the University of Glasgow

summary: Research on how cognitive empathy develops across the lifespan, and the challenges facing children with neurological disorders and neurodiverse profiles.
description: Professor Liam Dorris, a distinguished paediatric neuropsychologist and honorary professor at the University of Glasgow, provides insights into his latest research to describe the development of cognitive empathy across the lifespan. The discussion highlights the importance of empathy as a fundamental human ability for navigating social environments, with a particular focus on children with neurological disorders and neurodiverse profiles. Professor Dorris emphasises the challenges these children may face in developing mature empathy and the implications for support and intervention. He outlines how the latest research data can help frame our understanding of empathy at different stages of the life cycle and improve outcomes for patients and families. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2025 in Glasgow, Scotland.

title: Professor Nitin Kapur at RCPCH Conference 2025

speakers.name: Professor Nitin Kapur
speakers.role: President of the Paediatric & Child Health Division of the Royal Australasian College of Physicians

summary: A short greeting from an Australian visitor on the experience of seeing thousands of paediatricians gathered at the conference.
description: Professor Nitin Kapur, President of the Paediatric & Child Health Division of the Royal Australasian College of Physicians, shares his enthusiasm for the large gathering of paediatricians at the RCPCH conference. He expresses his excitement at seeing thousands of paediatricians in one room, a rare experience for him as an attendee from Australia, and wishes the RCPCH the very best for the future. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2025 in Glasgow, Scotland.

title: RCPCH Conference 2024: commitment to research

speakers.name: Professor Will Carroll
speakers.role: Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health joint officer for research

summary: An introduction to the annual conference and the commitment of UK paediatricians to research, with a focus on health inequalities.
description:
Professor Will Carroll, Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health joint officer for research, introduces the annual conference and highlights the commitment shown by paediatricians to research across the United Kingdom. A specific focus of the conference was on health inequalities which ties with the RCPCH mission and objectives.

This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK. These works are owned by the Paediatric Video Journal (PVJ) and are protected by copyright laws and treaties around the world. All rights are reserved.

title: Paediatric coeliac disease; more cases, more symptoms and fewer biopsies than before

speakers.name: Lydia Chapman
speakers.role: Cardiff University

summary: How coeliac disease diagnoses in children are shifting towards non-biopsy pathways, and whether the IgA-TTG threshold for diagnosis could be lowered.
description: Lydia Chapman, Cardiff University, discusses her work in investigating the number of paediatric patients diagnosed with coeliac disease via biopsy and non-biopsy pathways and comparing this to their IgA-TTG results. The main findings showed that there are more diagnoses occurring via non-biopsy approach. The team also identified that all patients diagnosed with an IgA-TTG greater than 5x ULN were diagnosed with coeliac disease and thus they question the possibility of lowering the non-biopsy diagnosis threshold. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK.

title: The Dr Me Project: student led workshops in empowering self-care in primary schools

speakers.name: Ivy Ng
speakers.role: Imperial College London

summary: A student-led school session teaching year 5 children about common minor illnesses and how to choose appropriate NHS services.
description: Ivy Ng, Imperial College London, discusses her work on 'The Dr Me Project' which aims to improve health literacy and education in primary school children. A group of students delivered an hour session to year 5 classes incorporating workshops on diarrhoea and vomiting, fever and sore throats. The team found the session to be well received by the children, with improvement in ability to select appropriate NHS services. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK.

title: Ethnic diversity of children and young people with ADHD

speakers.name: Tapomay Banerjee
speakers.role: Cambridgeshire Community Services NHS Trust

summary: How ethnic minority children are under-represented among those diagnosed with ADHD, and why targeted awareness work is needed.
description:
Tapomay Banerjee, Cambridgeshire Community Services NHS Trust, discusses his work on describing the ethnic distribution of children diagnosed with ADHD. Dr Banerjee and his team identified that despite the significant ethnic minority population in the areas where the research took place, the representation of ADHD was only between 2% to 5%. Targeted awareness and working with ethnic minority communities was highlighted to support the outcome and management of ADHD in these children.

This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK. These works are owned by the Paediatric Video Journal (PVJ) and are protected by copyright laws and treaties around the world. All rights are reserved.

title: A decade of UK accidental adrenaline auto-injector injury in children

speakers.name: Emily Hilton
speakers.role: Cardiff Medical School

summary: What a decade of poisons service enquiries shows about accidental adrenaline auto-injector injuries in children and how education may prevent them.
description: Emily Hilton, Cardiff Medical School, discusses her work in analysing enquiries to the National Poisons information service related to accidental adrenaline auto-injector injuries. In most cases, the symptoms of accidental injuries seemed to resolve spontaneously with a handful of cases requiring antidote treatment for ischaemia. Improved education regarding storage and safe use of AAIs for carers may reduce accidental injury in children. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK.

title: Transition services and developmentally appropriate healthcare for young people

speakers.name: Ria Patel
speakers.role: University College London

summary: How transition and developmentally appropriate healthcare is delivered across a regional paediatric network, with unequal access and wide variation.
description: Ria Patel, University College London, discusses her work assessing how transition and developmentally appropriate healthcare is being delivered accross the North Thames Paediatric Network in the UK. The team found that there is currently inequitable access to resources and support for healthcare professionals to provide transition and developmentally appropriate healthcare services accross the network with wide variation in service delivery. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK.

title: The impact of armed conflict on paediatric healthcare consultations in Northwest Syria

speakers.name: Vaibhavee Patel
speakers.role: University of Leeds

summary: How armed conflict and displacement in northwest Syria affect children's use of healthcare, and why aid needs to be tailored to need.
description: Vaibhavee Patel, University of Leeds, discusses her work in collaboration with the Syrian American Medical Society (SAMS) on the impact of armed conflict on healthcare, especially in children who are often the worst impacted. Ms Patel and her team found that as levels of displacement increased, there was a decrease in healthcare consultations for nutrition related disorders, trauma, non-communicable diseases and also more surprisingly infectious diseases. The study highlights that aid needs to be tailored for the needs and thus further research is needed to inform global health policy. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK.

title: Lumbar puncture toolkit for a children's hospital

speakers.name: Kosisochukwu Nwigwe
speakers.role: Sheffield Childrens' Hospital

summary: A lumbar puncture toolkit for a children's hospital, combining a departmental guideline, a patient information leaflet and a procedure box.
description:
Kosisochukwu Nwigwe, Sheffield Childrens' Hospital, discusses his work in producing a lumbar puncture toolkit comprised of a departmental guideline, a patient information leaflet and a lumbar puncture box.

This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK. These works are owned by the Paediatric Video Journal (PVJ) and are protected by copyright laws and treaties around the world. All rights are reserved.

title: Back to school - an exercise in social accountability for medical students

speakers.name: Professor Nick Makwana
speakers.role: Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust

summary: A partnership placing third-year medical students in primary schools in deprived areas to build social accountability into the medical curriculum.
description: Professor Nick Makwana, Sandwell and West Birmingham Hospitals NHS Trust, discusses his initiative in forming a partnership with the local education authority and University medical school to place 3rd year medical students in primary schools in areas of high deprivation index. This study  substantiates the need to incorporate social accountability into medical school curriculum. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK.

title: Antibiotic allergy documentation and referral in a university teaching hospital

speakers.name: Eva Wooding
speakers.role: Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust

summary: Why no children with a low-risk antibiotic allergy label were referred for delabelling, and why paediatric services need to improve this.
description: Eva Wooding, Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, discusses her work in assessing the appropriate uptake of penicillin allergy delabelling services in a University Teaching Hospital. The team found that referral to the paediatric antibiotic allergy de-labelling clinic was poor with 0% of 'low risk' allergies being referred. Further work needs to be carried out in paediatric services to support de-labelling of antibiotic allergies as we know fewer than 10% of people that believe they have an antibiotic allergy really do.. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK.

title: LocSSIPs in a paediatric intensive care setting

speakers.name: Kokul Sriskandarajah
speakers.role: London North West Healthcare Trust

summary: How consistently Local Safety Standards for Invasive Procedures are documented when inserting lines in paediatric intensive care, and what must improve.
description: Kokul Sriskandarajah, London North West Healthcare Trust, discusses his work in identifying the utilisation of Local Safety Standards for Invasive Procedures (LocSSIP) in the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit of large teaching hospital in London. Following 268 never events in the UK in 2023, LocSSIPs are seen as a fundamental part of ensuring safety when inserting lines in a PICU setting and is paramount for patient safety. The team found significant shortcomings in documentation of LocSSIPs with a clear need to educate medical staff and the better integration into local electronic systems. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK.

title: Screening of unaccompanied asylum seeking children and young persons

speakers.name: Agatha Okah
speakers.role: Birmingham Children's Hospital

summary: Findings from screening unaccompanied asylum seeking children: delays in investigations and communication, and low vitamin D levels.
description: Agatha Okah, Birmingham Children's Hospital, discusses her work on screening unaccompanied asylum seeking children and young persons (UASCYP) in Warwickshire. A recent surge in the number of UASCYP coming for check ups led to adverse events due to missed disease identification in these patients. Dr Okah and her team identified that there was a delay in investigations after screening and a further delay in communication for treatment. Incidental findings also showed low vitamin D levels identified in UASCYP. Recommendations were made based on these findings. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK.

title: Adherence to hydroxycarbamide in children with sickle cell disease

speakers.name: Eva Tsouana
speakers.role: Basildon Hospital

summary: How adherence to hydroxycarbamide was measured in children with sickle cell disease, and why patient-reported adherence ran higher than laboratory measures.
description: Eva Tsouana, Basildon Hospital, discusses her work in measuring adherence to hydroxycarbamide in paediatric patients with sickle cell disease. With a current lack of a standardised biomarker or objective assessment tool for measuring adherence, her team assessed adherence using various methodologies and they subsequently identified markers that may influence adherence based on patient and treatment characteristics. Patient-reported adherence were found to be higher than adherence assessed by laboratory markers and MPRs. Further research and qualitative interventions are needed to measure and improve adherence to hydroxycarbamide. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK.

title: Evaluation of association between snake bite and myocarditis among children

speakers.name: Arun Prasad
speakers.role: All India Institute of Medical Sciences

summary: Whether snake envenomation in children is linked to myocarditis, with a considerably higher incidence of cardiac complications found afterwards.
description: Arun Prasad, All India Institute of Medical Sciences, discusses his work in evaluating the association between myocarditis and snake envenomation in children. Dr Prasad and his team found a considerably higher incidence of cardiac complications in children after snake envenomation. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK.

title: Phoenix criteria for paediatric sepsis and septic shock - what is new?

speakers.name: Professor Mark Peters
speakers.role: UCL Great Ormond Street Institute for Child Health

summary: An overview of the Phoenix criteria for identifying sepsis and septic shock in children, and how they were developed and validated.
description: Professor Mark Peters, UCL Great Ormond Street Institute for Child Health, provides an overview of the Phoenix criteria for paediatric sepsis and septic shock. The Phoenix sepsis criteria for sepsis and septic shock in children were derived and validated by the international SCCM Paediatric Sepsis Definition Task Force using a large international database and survey, systematic review and meta-analysis, and modified Delphi consensus approach. A Phoenix Sepsis Score of at least 2 identified potentially life-threatening organ dysfunction in children younger than 18 years with infection, and its use has the potential to improve clinical care, epidemiological assessment, and research in paediatric sepsis and septic shock around the world. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK.

title: Registrar Ready: stimulation to educate, enlighten and empower

speakers.name: Nat Jansen
speakers.role: Health Education England

summary: How standardised, simulation-based Registrar Ready days give paediatric trainees in the North of England an equitable preparation for the tier 2 rota.
description: Nat Jansen, Health Education England, discusses his work in trying to provide an equitable experience for trainees undertaking the Registrar Ready days in the North of England. These days are aimed at trainees prior to starting the second on-call (tier 2) rota. Previous sessions were delivered on an ad-hoc basis and were variable depending on the location within the region. The team aimed to organise the training days in a more succinct fashion and to deliver more precisely. A simulation based medical education was incorporated in the course which trainees found to be relevant and improve their confidence when they take responsibility in real life clinical situations. Standardising has meant that paediatric trainees have an equitable experience when attending the course. The authors hope to integrate this into regional recommendations as part of "readiness for tier 2 rota" e-portfolio entry. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK.

title: RCPCH Conference 2024: working better together

speakers.name: Neil Meemaduma
speakers.role: Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health

summary: The aim of this year's conference, working better together, and the chance for members to present research, audits and quality improvement work.
description:
Neil Meemaduma, Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health, discusses the aim of this years conference; 'working better together'. As associate director for research and quality improvement, he describes the opportunity provided for members to present research, audits and quality improvement studies. A specific focus of the conference was on health inequalities which ties with the RCPCH mission and objectives.

This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK. These works are owned by the Paediatric Video Journal (PVJ) and are protected by copyright laws and treaties around the world. All rights are reserved.

title: Baseline characteristics and clinical profile of children presenting with TB disease

speakers.name: Aniqah Hossain
speakers.role: Royal London Hospital

summary: The characteristics and clinical profile of children with TB disease at a large East London NHS trust, where pulmonary TB was the most common form.
description: Aniqah Hossain, Royal London Hospital, discusses her work in describing the characteristics and clinical profile of children presenting with TB disease to a large NHS Trust in East London. In the predominantly south Asian cohort, female predominance was seen. Pulmonary TB was the most common clinical phenotype found. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK.

title: The impact of undergraduate medical conferences on medical student choice of speciality

speakers.name: Syeda Bilgrami
speakers.role: King's College London

speakers.name: Ilayda Okten
speakers.role: King's College London

summary: How an undergraduate medical conference was organised to give students more exposure to paediatrics and its career pathway.
description: Syeda Bilgrami and Ilayda Okten, King's College London, discuss their work in organising an undergraduate medical conference; 'Milestones To Go: Accessibility and Development within Paediatrics' to try and improve medical student exposure to the paediatric speciality. The conference managed to introduce the paediatric speciality pathway to aspiring paediatricians to fill the gap in the medical curriculum and develop undergraduate understanding of a paediatric career. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK.

title: Why people choose not to be vaccinated?

speakers.name: David Tuthill
speakers.role: Cardiff and Vale University Health Board

summary: Why some families choose not to vaccinate their children, with refusal largely driven by media misinformation and worries about side effects.
description: David Tuthill, Cardiff and Vale University Health Board, discusses his work carried out in collaboration with Public Health Wales and The Children's Hospital for Wales to try and identify why families choose not to vaccinate their children. Dr Tuthill and his team found that most refusal to vaccination by families was not supported by scientific facts and mainly driven by media misinformation and worries about side effects. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK.

title: Are referrals for suspected paediatric bone and soft tissue tumours meeting the two week standard?

speakers.name: Binod Pander
speakers.role: Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital

summary: Whether referrals for suspected bone and soft tissue tumours meet the two-week cancer standard, and where delays in the pathway occur.
description: Binod Pander, Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital, discusses his work in identifying if cancer pathway standards are being met in a tertiary referral centre in London. The standards are being adhered to in terms of reviewing patients within the two week time frame and diagnosing within 28 days. However, a delay was identified in initiation of cancer treatment. Furthermore, lots of cases of benign osteochondroma have been identified as potentially leading to delay for other more important cases. Further discussions are needed to streamline the pathway for these benign cases. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK.

title: Complications in adolescent Hodgkin's lymphoma patients with PICC lines

speakers.name: Rebecca Howitt
speakers.role: University of Oxford

summary: Complication rates of PICC lines in adolescents with Hodgkin's lymphoma, including mechanical problems that can delay treatment.
description: Rebecca Howitt, University of Oxford, discusses her work on PICC line complication rates in adolescent Hodgkin's Lymphoma patients. The team at Oxford continue to have a positive experience with PICC lines regarding quality of life and patient acceptability. However, Rebecca and her team found that mechanical complications of PICC lines remain a clinical concern, often leading to treatment delays. Ultimately, larger studies are needed to develop strategies to minimise PICC line complications. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK.

title: Patterns of mental health admissions amongst children and young people

speakers.name: Joseph Ward
speakers.role: University College London

summary: How hospital admissions for mental health problems in UK young people have risen, mostly among girls aged 11 to 15 and those with eating disorders.
description: Joseph Ward, University College London, discusses his work on analysing hospital admissions due to mental health issues in children and young people in the UK. Dr Ward and his team found that mental health admissions had increased by 60 to 70% in young people, mostly driven by 11 to 15 year old females and those with eating disorders. A greater understanding of these findings is thought to be realised through the MAPS study which this project is one element of. This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK.

title: Metabolic dysfunction associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) in children: use of FibroScan

speakers.name: Caitlin Murphy
speakers.role: King's College Hospital

summary: How fibroscan measures of liver stiffness and steatosis were assessed in 76 children with MASLD, most of whom had steatosis and mild fibrosis.
description: Caitlin Murphy, King's College Hospital, discusses her work in identifying identifying fibroscan markers of liver stiffness and steatosis, with anthriopometry, ultrasound and biochemical liver functions tests in 76 children with MASLD. The majority of children were found to have evidence of significant steatosis and mild fibrosis, both of which are completely reversible at the stage of identification.  This interview took place at the RCPCH conference 2024 in Birmingham, UK.
